title: Stability assertions and IO invariants for locked model releases
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Define a machine- and human-readable set of stability assertions (IO invariants + performance tolerances) that we publish alongside any 'locked' model version. These assertions will be used by onboarding flows, the runtime validation harness, and the Console release page. Goal: lower surprise for customers who pin to a model version by guaranteeing minimal changes in prompt shape, structured outputs, and latency/throughput profiles.
acceptance_criteria: A1: A normative spec (markdown) exists that enumerates: input schema expectations, stable output fields, optional fields and their stability levels, and parameter semantics (temperature, top_p) for locked versions.

A2: A CI validation harness is runnable that takes a candidate model binary and verifies: prompt-format conformance, no-breaking-output-field-removals, tokenization parity checks, and per-scenario latency regression thresholds. The harness returns machine-readable pass/fail results.

A3: Performance profile publishing pipeline produces a JSON profile for each locked model with 50th/95th/99th latency, tokens/sec at typical batch sizes, and memory footprint. Published profiles are visible in Console and surfaced via the catalog API.

A4: Rollback/fallback policy documented: if a locked release fails any assertion in production telemetry for two consecutive deploys or exceeds the regression threshold, an automated fallback to the previous pinned-compatible variant is triggered and paging is sent to oncall.
A5: Documentation and quickstart for partners that shows how to consume assertions programmatically and how to pin safely in Redwood Dedicated/Private.
A6: Backcompat test coverage added to release pipeline with representative prompt set (covered prompts > 300 unique prompt templates) and automated diff reports stored in the release artifact.
A7: Design review and signoff from PM and Runtime leads recorded in the ticket.
A8: A migration path for minor output schema additions (stable: additive fields allowed flagged as 'opt-in') is specified with examples.
A9: Dashboard alerts (Console) for customer-facing regressions (quality / latency) wired to the release page and to the SRE alerting rules repository.
A10: Security review note if model includes encrypted artifacts or non-standard tokenizers (flagged at onboarding time).

2026-03-14: Assigned to Liam for engineering work; SRE contacted to review alert thresholds next week.
decisions: D1: We will publish two classes of assertions: 'IO invariants' (strict guarantees) and 'Performance tolerances' (best-effort thresholds with regression alerts).
D2: Tokenizer parity check is mandatory for any locked model; builds will fail onboarding if tokenization mapping differs beyond a small threshold for shared vocabulary.

D3: Additive output fields are allowed but must be marked 'optional' in the IO spec and included in the example outputs. Removing or renaming existing output fields is a breaking change and disallowed for locked versions.

D4: Parameter semantics (temperature, top_p) must document how defaults map to sampling behavior; we will capture canonical sampling outputs for a small set of seeding prompts as part of the release artifact.

D5: Performance profiles will be published in JSON under a stable URL schema: /catalog/models/:model_id/versions/:version/perf.json. Console integration will fetch and render the 50/95/99 latency bands.

QA_plan: Run harness on canary cluster with traffic replay for a week to validate false-positive rate of regressions.
Create synthetic regression tests that intentionally violate IO invariants to validate alerts and rollback behavior.
Compare tokenization fingerprints across checkpoints and produce delta report; require manual review if > 2% of tokens remapped.
Include human evaluation step for 50 sampled prompts to detect semantic drift not captured by field-level invariants.
rollout_strategy: Canary rollout for locked-model publishing: initial publish to internal catalog, run harness + telemetry for 48h under 10% traffic, then progressively enable at 25/50/100% with automated rollback on two consecutive alert failures.
notes: This ticket focuses on the 'locked' model path used by customers who pin a version. For non-locked models we may provide looser compatibility notes. Coordinate closely with Dedicated/Private onboarding to ensure assertions are consumable in air-gapped environments (include offline artifacts).
